properties.statement: TWO SURFACES SHARE THE NAME `create_node` AND HAVE OPPOSITE SEMANTICS, and every consumer-facing document describes the wrong one. The MCP TOOL `create_node` MERGES: crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/query.rs:64 calls `g.upsert_node(...)`, and its own tool description says so ("An existing id MERGES: the props you pass overwrite, every stored property you omit survives"). The RUST method `DesignGraph::create_node` REPLACES (graph.rs:220, "Create (or replace)"). An agent can only call the tool; it cannot call the method. THREE PLACES TELL THE AGENT THE METHOD'S SEMANTICS FOR THE TOOL: (1) the served `revise-design` SKILL — "Do NOT reach for the generic `create_node` to revise. It is create-or-replace, so passing only the changed field resets every other property to its schema default — which silently downgrades an `accepted` requirement to `proposed`, reopens a settled Decision, and drops an artifact's checksum." (2) ver:constructors-preserve's description — "create_node and import_graph deliberately still REPLACE". (3) crates/reflow2-core/tests/upsert.rs module doc. MEASURED FALSE 2026-08-07 on invented nodes in a throwaway graph, using the skill's own scare case: a Requirement set to status=accepted, then `create_node` with props={statement} ALONE. Result — statement changed, and status stayed "accepted"; name, priority, provenance, concern, designation, kind and lineage all survived. Nothing was reset. Confirmed twice more in ordinary use the same day, on a TemporalFact updated with one property at a time. CONTRADICTED WITHIN THE GRAPH ITSELF: chg:merge-integrity-bl47-bl46 records "create_node on an existing id merges instead of replacing (the revise-design contract, now real)" — so the fix landed and the documents were never followed. ver:constructors-preserve PASSES while its description misstates this, and it can: grep shows the test asserts nothing about create_node at all. WHAT IT COSTS, hit today rather than imagined: several node types have NO typed constructor — TemporalFact is one, and TemporalFact is what dec:defects-are-temporal-facts makes the standard way to record a defect found by use. For those, `create_node` is the ONLY route, and the skill tells the agent that taking it will destroy the node. An agent that believes the skill either does not record the defect or passes a whole property set it had to reconstruct by hand, risking the very reset it was avoiding. The skill's advice (prefer typed constructors) stays right; the REASON given for it is false, and the reason is what an agent reasons from when the advice does not cover its case.
